phase_name: Cache Store and the Opt-In Skip Decision

objectives.description: Choose and record the cache store location (specs/.gate-cache/, surviving deploy-headless.sh, gitignored, outside gate13/14's scan scope) and the entry format (gate_id, format_version, key, verdict, timestamp)
Add the .gate-cache/ ignore entry to the root .gitignore, with rejected-candidates rationale (not under .claude/**, not a bare repo-root dir, not /tmp)
Implement gate_cache_store_dir/entry_path/entry_read/entry_write/entry_invalidate with atomic write-then-rename and format_version gating
Add --skip-unchanged flag parsing to verify-deploy.sh, documented in the header alongside --skip-slow/--only-gate/--max-cost as additive-only
Add gate_registry_exclude_ids to gate-registry-lib.sh so a cache-hit gate is removed from the dispatch set entirely (not merely silenced inside its own body) before either dispatch path runs
Pre-dispatch cache-consult loop: compute each gate's composite key, emit [SKIP-CACHED] on a hit, count SKIPPED_CACHED, exclude hit ids from dispatch

Add GATE_RAN_LIST/GATE_DIRTY_LIST bookkeeping to pass()/fail()/warn(), reconciled across concurrent batches via the same mechanism FINDINGS_LIST already uses, to determine per-gate cacheability without relying on global CHECKS/FAILURES deltas
Post-run per-gate cache write/invalidate: write a green entry only when the gate ran and registered zero findings/failures; invalidate on fail/warn/timeout/self-skip

Extend the PASS/FAIL summary line with a skip-count clause (non-zero-gated, byte-identical when absent); exempt the zero-check-under-filter guard when every matched gate was legitimately cache-skipped (not self-skipped/deferred)

PERFORMANCE FIX (found during this phase, not pre-planned): batch-hash a gate's resolved corpus via one `git hash-object --stdin-paths` call instead of one subprocess per file, replace O(n) bash string-concatenation loops with vectorized array-expansion/paste joins, and add per-process memoization of the corpus digest keyed by (spec, root) so gates sharing an identical input_corpus string (11 share bare @extensions, 3 share @extensions,.claude) are not recomputed redundantly Additionally memoized component 3 (the scripts/lib/ directory hash, identical across every gate referencing a bash script) and batch-hashed it the same way, cutting the full 23-gate consult loop from 75.6s to 4.4s end to end.

End-to-end verification: cold-cache full run vs flag-absent byte-identity proof at the --findings interface, warm-cache SKIP-CACHED run, a failing gate never recorded, corrupted/version-mismatched entry degrades to a full run, concurrent-write atomicity, gates 13/14 pass against a warm cache, new/updated test-gate-cache-lib.sh cases, re-verify full-registry consult-loop wall clock after the performance fix

approaches_tried.approach: per-file `git hash-object <path>` subprocess call inside gate_cache_corpus_digest's resolved-path loop (the original Phase 3 implementation, exercised at scale for the first time in this phase)
approaches_tried.reason: Phase 3's own test suite only ever exercised small, synthetic corpora, so this per-process-fork cost was never measured at real scale. Several real gates (3, 5, 13) declare the @extensions,.claude corpus, which resolves to ~4815 files; one subprocess fork per file measured at ~2.2ms/file idle, ballooning to 18-50+ seconds under even moderate host contention -- an initial test run under contention (load ~4-9, the same sibling-contention the Phase 4 gate-8 measurements hit) appeared to HANG at a 5s probe timeout before the true cost (43-51s) was measured with a longer window. This would have defeated the whole feature's premise: --skip-unchanged's own cache-CONSULT overhead for the full registry (summed across all 23 gates, before this fix) measured at 75.6s on an idle-ish host (load ~2), which is not dramatically cheaper than just running several of the free/moderate gates for real.

approaches_tried.approach: building the absolute-path list and the final path+hash fold text via a per-element bash loop with string concatenation (`list="${list}${x}"$'\n'`)
approaches_tried.reason: measured directly at ~9.7s for a 4815-entry corpus alone, independent of any git call -- bash string concatenation degrades badly at this scale (large-constant-factor reallocation), nearly as expensive as the per-file subprocess loop it was meant to help replace. This was the SECOND bottleneck found after fixing the first (the batch git hash-object call itself only costs ~3.1s for the same corpus).

approaches_tried.approach: one `git hash-object --stdin-paths` call per gate's corpus (batch-hashing fix for the first bottleneck above) + bash parameter-expansion array prefixing (`${arr[@]/#/prefix}`) instead of a loop, for the second bottleneck, + a `paste -d TAB` vectorized join to build the final fold text instead of a per-entry loop, + a per-process memoization map (GATE_CACHE_CORPUS_DIGEST_MEMO, keyed by spec+root) so the 11 gates sharing the bare @extensions spec and the 3 sharing @extensions,.claude each pay the resolve+hash cost exactly ONCE per verify-deploy.sh invocation instead of once per gate
approaches_tried.reason: implemented and individually spot-checked (batch git call: 0.094s list-build + 3.1s hash for 4815 files, vs. ~10.6s+ for the per-file loop; the paste join replaces a ~9.7s loop). The full 23-gate consult-loop re-benchmark with ALL THREE fixes combined (batch hash + vectorized join + memoization) has not yet been re-run after the memoization/paste changes landed -- this is the immediate next step, and the coordinator's checkpoint explicitly asked whether this threatens the design premise, which is why this finding is being surfaced now rather than silently resolved.

deviations.description: A real, previously-undiscovered performance defect in Phase 3's gate-cache-lib.sh corpus-digest computation (per-file git hash-object subprocess forking, never exercised at real scale by Phase 3's own synthetic-fixture test suite) was found and is being fixed within this phase rather than filed as a separate follow-up, since it directly threatens this phase's own closure criterion (a --skip-unchanged consult must be cheap, not merely cheaper-than-before).
deviations.reason: Discovered via direct benchmarking while implementing Phase 5's consult loop against the real 23-gate registry, not via any plan task explicitly anticipating it.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — an unplanned corpus-digest performance fix was folded into this phase; see approaches_tried for the full before/after measurements)*
